Ashley Moody

Republican candidate for United States Senator, Florida · Incumbent

U.S. Senator from Florida (incumbent, appointed 2025); attorney

Ashley Moody is a Republican and Florida's junior U.S. senator. Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed her in January 2025 to fill the seat Marco Rubio vacated, and before that she was Florida's attorney general from 2019 to 2025. She is running in the November 3, 2026 special election for the rest of the term against Democrat Angie Nixon and Neil J. Gillespie (NPA).

Where Moody stands

Immigration and border security
Supports stricter immigration enforcement, including finishing the border wall, ending sanctuary cities, and fighting human trafficking and drug smuggling.
Deportation of immigrants convicted of crimes
Supports expanding expedited removal for some immigrants convicted of crimes.
Public safety and criminal justice
Supports law enforcement and tougher criminal penalties, pointing to her record as a judge, federal prosecutor and state attorney general.
Health care
Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which included changes to Medicaid. Voted against extending the health care subsidies tied to the Affordable Care Act.
Medicaid / program fraud
Sponsored the HCBS Anti-Fraud Reporting Act of 2026 (S.5609), introduced September 30, 2026, which deals with fraud reporting in home- and community-based services.
Campaign platform
Is running on an 'America First' agenda focused on immigration and border security, crime and law enforcement, and the economy.

Background

  • U.S. Senator from Florida, 2025–present (appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis; took office January 21, 2025)
  • 38th Attorney General of Florida, 2019–2025
  • Judge, Thirteenth Judicial Circuit Court of Florida (Hillsborough County), 2007–2017
  • Former Assistant U.S. Attorney, Middle District of Florida; earlier worked in civil litigation
  • Education: University of Florida (BS, MS, JD); Stetson University (LLM)
  • Born March 28, 1975, in Plant City, Florida
